item.research_question: What are the optimization strategies of high-entropy alloys for electrocatalytic applications?
item.material_system: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) composed of five or more equiatomic or near-equiatomic components
item.processing_route: Various methods including carbon thermal shock, moving bed pyrolysis, magnetron sputtering, electrodeposition, and dealloying
key_findings: HEAs have a highly disordered structure and a wide range of composition modulation, showing excellent performance in mechanical properties, magnetic properties, and electrocatalysis
HEAs have abundant active sites, high selectivity, and high stability, making them ideal catalytic materials in electrocatalytic reactions
The high entropy effect, slow diffusion effect, lattice distortion effect, and cocktail effect of HEAs contribute to their unique properties and performance
Element regulation, defect regulation, and strain engineering are effective strategies for optimizing HEA catalysts
item.mechanism: The high entropy effect, slow diffusion effect, lattice distortion effect, and cocktail effect of HEAs contribute to their unique properties and performance
item.future_work: Further research is needed to explore the potential of HEAs in electrocatalytic applications and to develop more efficient synthesis methods and optimization strategies
quotes: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are expected to become one of the most promising functional materials in the field of electrocatalysis
The high entropy effect is a hallmark concept of HEAs, that is, five or more elements are uniformly mixed with a nearly equal molar ratio

key_findings: HEAs have shown potential in electrocatalytic research due to their excellent combined properties
